faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage suitable for Lumbar interbody fusion cage with porous lattice?
faq.a: Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage uses Ti-6Al-4V ELI because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address spine fixation operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for lumbar interbody fusion requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. lumbar interbody fusion components require Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for lumbar interbody fusion application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Spinal Interbody Cage includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet lumbar interbody fusion specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.
